newsitem.title: UK: Barclays' BZW has poor '96 FX performance.
newsitem.headline: Barclays' BZW has poor '96 FX performance.

text.p: Foreign exchange operations at BZW, the investment banking arm of Barclays Plc, performed disappointingly in 1996, the bank said on Tuesday.
"The foreign exchange business performed poorly in an increasingly competitive market," Barclays said in a statement accompanying full-year results.
The bank said operating profit at BZW slid by 29 percent to 204 million stg from 1995's 289 million stg, though it declined to specify the exact level of currency trading profits.
Overall, Barclays' 1996 pretax profit rose 13 percent to 2.36 billion stg, at the lower end of analysts' expectations.
The bank said performance in the fixed income business was disappointing, with the exception of sterling.
Income at BZW rose by seven percent, but costs increased by 18 percent year-on-year, Barclays said.
"The rise in costs reflected the continued substantial investment in people and systems, aimed at lifting profitability over the medium term," the statement said.
A new senior management team was installed in 1996 with the goal of improving performance of the business, it added.

Last week, Lloyds TSB Group Plc reported a 45 percent fall in 1996 dealing profits. Foreign exchange income dropped to 113 million stg from 122 million, while income from securities and other trading slumped by 70 million stg to a loss of 17 million from a 53 million profit in 1995.
Lloyds TSB's slide in dealing profits came amid a 52 percent jump in 1996 overall pre-tax profit to 2.505 billion stg.
